newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian state sugar firm sold to French group.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian state sugar firm sold to French group.

text.p: Ivory Coast has sold a majority stake in part of its state sugar firm Societe pour le Developpement des Plantations de Canne a Sucre (SODESUCRE) to a French-led consortium, the government said in a statement published on Thursday.

The consortium comprised Societe des Brasseries et Glacieres Internationales (BGI), Matignon Investissement et Gestion and Sucreries d'Ertein, a full statement of decisions taken at Wednesday's cabinet meeting said.

These firms would pay 8.129 billion CFA francs ($14 million) for lot A of SODESUCRE and take on attached debts totalling 3.030 billion CFA francs, according to the statement published in the government daily newspaper Fraternite Matin.
Another consortium led by Ivorian commodities group SIFCA would take a 55 percent shareholding in lot B of SODESUCRE, which is being privatised as two separate blocs.
The consortium would pay 16.8 billion CFA francs and had agreed to take on two billion CFA of attached debts, according to an earlier statement issued late on Wednesday.
SIFCA's consortium partners are Mauritian sugar firm Harel freres and another firm, Rial Trading, the statement said.
Both lots A and B comprise two production plants and surounding plantations.
Ivory Coast had said it would retain a 20 percent stake in SODESUCRE. Another 20 percent stake be floated on Abidjan's bourse and employees would take the remaining five percent.
Senegal's Cie Sucriere Senegalaise had also put in a bid for lot B, which is made up of plants in northwest and central Ivory Coast.
Bidders for lot A included a group comprising British commodities trader ED & F Man Group PLC and Britain's Commonwealth Development Corporation, an overseas finance institution.
